sota_to_phase_d_mapping.implementation_delta: Rerun the clean D3 MuSR selector with an uncertainty head over the EBRM score, then penalize high-variance candidates before comparing against tuned self-consistency. If D1 is retried, attach the same calibration head to the LoRA-EBM scorer.
sota_to_phase_d_mapping.pitfall: The evidence is RLHF/preference-domain calibration, not a direct reasoning-selector win; style or safety uncertainty could be mistaken for reasoning correctness.
sota_to_phase_d_mapping.source_signal: Adds conformal uncertainty and heteroscedastic reward variance to avoid over-weighting unreliable RM scores.

sota_to_phase_d_mapping.implementation_delta: Replace the scalar D3 energy readout with a reward-distribution head and sweep pessimistic beta values on the existing MuSR candidate cache before any second-corpus spend.
sota_to_phase_d_mapping.pitfall: This is a unifying objective, not a finished verifier; excessive pessimism can abstain away the exact headroom D3 needs to capture.
sota_to_phase_d_mapping.source_signal: Frames the right reward object as a distribution p(r|x,y), with pessimistic log-moment aggregation for uncertain regions.

sota_to_phase_d_mapping.implementation_delta: Insert a RewardUQ-style calibration table into the D1/D3 harness: ECE, AUROC on correct-vs-incorrect candidates, and selection delta after uncertainty-aware abstention.
sota_to_phase_d_mapping.method: RewardUQ calibration harness for verifier uncertainty
sota_to_phase_d_mapping.pitfall: Better calibration can still leave selection accuracy tied with SC; the .462 gate must require delta_vs_tuned_sc, not calibration alone.
sota_to_phase_d_mapping.source_signal: Compares uncertainty quantification methods for reward models and ranks them by accuracy plus calibration.

sota_to_phase_d_mapping.implementation_delta: Add a matched-compute cascade control beside D1/D2/D3: cheap verifier selects when confident, uncertain pairs go to the same LLM-judge budget already used as a comparator.
sota_to_phase_d_mapping.pitfall: The judge can become the real verifier if cost and oracle-distinct boundaries are not charged explicitly; a win must separate cheap verifier value from judge fallback value.
sota_to_phase_d_mapping.source_signal: Routes uncertain preference pairs from a cheap RM to a stronger judge, improving cost-quality tradeoffs over random judge calls.

sota_to_phase_d_mapping.implementation_delta: Use LC-ERD as the D2 unblock path when next-token logprob caches are missing: derive process utility from consistency-regulated latent logic across the existing candidate batch, then compare to tuned SC.
sota_to_phase_d_mapping.pitfall: Endogenous consensus can preserve generator bias and create a model-identity shortcut, so the no-model-id adversarial check stays mandatory.
sota_to_phase_d_mapping.source_signal: Mines latent logic and decomposes step utility from consistency signals when explicit process labels are scarce.
